profile.summary: OpenSpliceAI predicts splice sites from DNA sequence. It is a PyTorch reimplementation of SpliceAI that scores every position as a donor site, an acceptor site or neither, and can also score how genetic variants change splicing. It ships a human model retrained on GRCh38 with MANE annotations, models for four other species, and tools to train new models.
profile.summary_source_locator: README.md: introduction, Key Features; paper: Results

summary_quotes.text: It is a reimplementation and extension of SpliceAI (Jaganathan et al., 2019) built on the modern PyTorch framework.
OpenSpliceAI assigns a score to each position that is an estimate of the probability that the position is a donor site, acceptor site, or neither
OpenSpliceAI not only predicts splice sites but also assesses the impact of genetic variants (SNPs and INDELs) on splicing.
updated from GRCh37 to GRCh38 using the latest MANE annotations

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: OpenSpliceAI keeps the SpliceAI design: a deep residual convolutional neural network that reads one-hot encoded DNA. In the 10,000 nt model the input passes through an initial Conv1D layer and 16 residual units with skip connections, then a softmax gives, for each position, the probability of donor, acceptor or neither. Smaller variants use fewer residual units (12 for 2000 nt, 8 for 400 nt). The input is padded with 5000 Ns on each side. For each flanking length five models were trained with different random seeds, and their outputs are averaged as an ensemble. The variant subcommand computes delta scores that measure how a variant changes splice site strength.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: The human model, OSAI-MANE, was released at four flanking lengths (80, 400, 2000 and 10000 nt), each as five checkpoint files (Model 1 to 5). The authors strongly recommend the 10000 nt model; the others are for experimental and research use. Species models exist for mouse, zebrafish, honey bee and thale cress. The README at the commit read shows version v.0.0.7. A result should name the species model, the flanking length, whether the five-model ensemble or a single seed was used, and the package version.

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Deep residual convolutional neural network: an initial Conv1D layer, then 16 residual units with skip connections in the 10,000 nt model (12 for 2000 nt, 8 for 400 nt), then a softmax over donor, acceptor and neither.

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: A genome FASTA file and a trained PyTorch model, with an optional GFF annotation; for variant scoring, a VCF file, FASTA and annotation. Sequences are one-hot encoded internally.

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: Per-position donor and acceptor probabilities, written as BED files of predicted donor and acceptor sites (the quick start page also mentions a GFF file); the variant subcommand writes a VCF with delta scores.

strengths.text: Retrainable: the package includes subcommands to build training data from a FASTA and GFF, train from scratch, fine-tune the human model for another species, and calibrate outputs.

quotes.text: Converts genome FASTA and annotation (GFF/GTF) files into one-hot encoded datasets (HDF5 format) for training and testing.
Fine-tunes a pre-trained human model for other species, reducing training time and improving performance on species with limited data.
Adjusts model output probabilities to better reflect true splice site likelihoods

strengths.text: The human model is retrained on GRCh38 with MANE annotations, where the original SpliceAI was trained on GENCODE V24lift37 transcripts on hg19/GRCh37.

quotes.text: which was trained using the canonical transcripts from GENCODE version V24lift37 from the hg19/GRCh37 reference genome.
updated from GRCh37 to GRCh38 using the latest MANE annotations

strengths.text: The authors report faster processing and lower memory use than the original SpliceAI code, enough to analyse large genomic regions on a single GPU.

quotes.text: Our experiments show that it achieves faster processing speeds and lower memory usage than the original SpliceAI code, allowing large-scale analyses of extensive genomic regions on a single GPU.

limitations.text: Scores depend on strand and flanking context. Feeding a short gene FASTA on its own pads it with N and scores minus-strand genes on the wrong strand, which the authors say collapses scores to near zero. Pass the whole chromosome with a GFF, or add 5,000 bp each side yourself.

quotes.text: If you instead feed a short, standalone gene FASTA, the sequence is padded with ``N`` and minus-strand genes are scored on the wrong strand — both of which collapse the scores to near zero.

run_guide.summary: Install OpenSpliceAI, get the human MANE 10,000 nt models from the repository, and predict splice sites on chromosome 22.
prerequisites: Python 3.9 or higher, and compilers. PyTorch is installed as a dependency (torch >= 2.2.1).
Optional NVIDIA GPU with drivers and CUDA toolkit for acceleration. Memory needs are not stated.
Code is GPL-3.0. No separate weights licence is stated.

steps.title: Download the example genome and annotation
steps.shell:
mkdir -p data
curl -o data/chr22.fa ftp://ftp.ccb.jhu.edu/pub/data/OpenSpliceAI/data/chr22.fa
curl -o data/chr22.gff ftp://ftp.ccb.jhu.edu/pub/data/OpenSpliceAI/data/chr22.gff
steps.explanation: Fetches the chromosome 22 FASTA and annotation that the quick start page links to. The mkdir and curl lines are added; the page gives only the download links.

quotes.text: ftp://ftp.ccb.jhu.edu/pub/data/OpenSpliceAI/data/chr22.fa
ftp://ftp.ccb.jhu.edu/pub/data/OpenSpliceAI/data/chr22.gff

steps.title: Predict splice sites
steps.shell:
openspliceai predict \
    -m models/openspliceai-mane/10000nt/ \
    -o results \
    -f 10000 \
    -i data/chr22.fa \
    -a data/chr22.gff \
    -t 0.9
steps.explanation: The quick start command, with the model directory path changed from 10000nt/ to the repository's models/openspliceai-mane/10000nt/ as the page says to adapt filenames. -f 10000 matches the 10,000 nt model, and -a lets the tool score each gene on its own strand with genomic flanking.

quotes.text: openspliceai predict \ -m 10000nt/ \ -o results \ -f 10000 \ -i data/chr22.fa \ -a data/chr22.gff \ -t 0.9
